page.title: Day 9 against Neave's manual
page.standfirst_html: Every flag the comparator raised for Day 9, adjudicated against L.Day.9.15Feb22.pdf — the extracted text for wording, and eighteen page images for emphasis, colour and the two things pdftotext cannot show at all. The headline is on printed p20: a ~300-word passage of Neave's — his "explain this item to a friend" exercise, which he frames as preparation for the final Major Activity on Day 12 — is absent from the site, and in its place stand two invented paragraphs, one of which attributes a fabricated quotation to Neave himself on "Day 2 page 16" (a page that is actually a Pause for Thought about a control chart). Elsewhere: the whole "Approvals, Acknowledgments and Information" page is missing — three third-party permission statements, including the one covering the Scherkenbach diagram the site reproduces; Neave's own comments are printed in Deming-blue in four places; John's letter has its second paragraph pushed outside the quotation; a Day 1 cross-reference points at page 25 instead of page 35; and "still", "rather", "own", "as", "if" and the clause "it takes time." are each dropped from a sentence. There is also a systematic emphasis problem: 29 paragraphs have lost italics the source carries, and three have gained italics it does not. Decide each one; export the file; I make the edits and open the PR.

items.source_html:
Printed p20, first paragraph (≈300 words): “If your initial reaction was something like the first two suggested above, ‘Really important’ or ‘I’m already familiar with this’, what then? … Imagine that you are with a friend who has not been working on this course but has been quite interested in the little that you have so far told him about it. I can personally heartily endorse that statement.”

Printed p20 then continues straight to “Other suggestions for what you might include…” — there is no further paragraph.
items.site_html:
line 84: "If your initial reaction was 'I'm already familiar with this', fine, but don't just leave it at that! Particularly if it's a topic on which you are at this stage quite knowledgeable, write a brief explanation of it---maybe one or two or three sentences. One benefit is that, later on, if you've forgotten some of the detail, your explanation could save some time. More importantly, writing an explanation will help with further thinking: for example, a very useful thought would be "Yes, and not only that ..."! If nothing else, do as Deming would have done---think and ask---and observe how the item relates to other topics throughout the System of Profound Knowledge."

line 86 (entirely absent from the source): "More suggestions on how to proceed will be given in the individual Sections. … you might lose heart. … Look at the brighter side … Meanwhile, recall what I said on Day 2 page 16: "Don't only think that you don't know---think about what you do know!""
items.proposal:
If your initial reaction was something like the first two suggested above, "Really important" or "I'm already familiar with this", what then? You could, of course, move straight on to the next item. However, I have a suggestion for such cases, a suggestion that will in fact be extremely useful preparation for when you reach the final Major Activity of the course at the end of Day 12. Imagine that you are with a friend who has not been working on this course but has been quite interested in the little that you have so far told him about it. (It would be particularly useful to choose a friend who is also part of "your organisation" so that references to what happens there, or doesn't happen, would be helpful.) Your friend has, of course, not previously been exposed to Deming's style of writing. First, and if necessary, see if you can translate the item into a form which your friend *can* understand! Naturally, you will almost certainly need to include a larger amount of description, and you will have to use words in ways with which you and your friend are *both* familiar. There is, of course, no reason why you shouldn't refer directly to what Deming wrote as well: there's no harm in introducing your friend to that style of writing as you explain things to him---he might get interested in reading some of Deming's work himself before long, and you'll have helped get him off to a great start! Following the translation (if needed), explain to your friend why Deming is including this item and what's important about it. Basically I'm suggesting that, for those items in Deming's writing that you are already fairly happy about, you have a little practice here for preparing to teach somebody else about it. It has often been said that the best way to really understand something is to teach it to others! I can personally heartily endorse that statement.

[…and DELETE the invented paragraph currently at line 86 entirely.]
items.evidence_html:
This is the headline finding of the pass. Confirmed word-for-word against the page image, printed p20. The source's ~300-word “explain it to a friend” passage — which Neave explicitly frames as preparation for the final Major Activity on Day 12 — is absent from the site in any form (grep -rn "friend" content/days/day-09/ finds it only as the one-line bullet on the p29 summary, where the source also has it). In its place stand two paragraphs with no counterpart anywhere in the PDF.

The second of them is the more serious: it attributes a quotation, “Don't only think that you don't know—think about what you do know!”, to Neave on Day 2 page 16, styles it .deming_quote, and hyperlinks it. The phrase appears nowhere in this corpus outside this one line (grep -rn "think about what you do know" content/ → one hit, this line), and Day 2's #sec-page16 is Pause for Thought 2–e, about reading a control chart. The citation is invented as well as the quotation. Same shape as Day 8's 05-introduction-to-the-major-activity.qmd:64.

items.proposal:
### Approvals, Acknowledgments and Information

^a^ ([page 3, Deming's Queen Elizabeth Conference Centre presentation](02-a-system.qmd#sec-page3)) Dr Deming's presentation at the Queen Elizabeth Conference Centre in London in July 1990 is fully transcribed in the Deming A5 Booklet A10 (formally BDA Booklet A10): *Deming Speaks to European Executives*, available from the Deming Transformation Forum: [www.deming.org.uk](https://www.deming.org.uk).

^b^ ([page 9, the Scherkenbach "boxes and lines" diagram](03-activity-9c-and-organisation-charts.qmd#sec-page9)) This diagram from *Deming's Road to Continual Improvement* has been reproduced with the approval of Bill Scherkenbach and SPC Press Inc.

^c^ ([page 11, the May 1990 System of Profound Knowledge extract](04-major-activity.qmd#sec-page12)) The May 1990 version of Dr Deming's System of Profound Knowledge which is used during Days 9--11 is fully transcribed in the Deming A5 Booklet A9 (formally BDA Booklet A9): *A System of Profound Knowledge*, available from the Deming Transformation Forum: [www.deming.org.uk](https://www.deming.org.uk).
items.evidence_html:
Confirmed on the page image, printed p31. This is not a site-wide omission: Days 5, 7 and 11 all reproduce their approvals pages (Day 11 in exactly the ^a^ ([page N, description](link)) … shape proposed here — and its note c is word-for-word the same Scherkenbach permission as Day 9's note b), and Days 1 and 6 carry theirs as Quarto footnote definitions. Day 9 has neither.

It matters more than a typical missing paragraph: these are rights and permission statements for third-party material the site reproduces — the Scherkenbach diagram on printed p9 is on the site as org-chart-complex.png. It also repairs a dangling reference: printed p11 says “(see the information at c on page 31)”, and there is currently no page 31 to see.

Together with the hyphen artifacts these are extraction defects, not site defects: the site is right and the comparator's input is wrong. Known false-positive classes from Days 3 and 4.

sections.title: Out of scope for this pass
sections.note_html: Genuine differences from the source that a single day's content pass is the wrong instrument for — cross-cutting presentation decisions and cross-day gaps. Recorded so they are visible rather than silently absorbed.

items.chip: Day 9 never uses `neave_note` for its small-print insets
items.flag: not flagged — presentation
items.source_html: Neave sets his own commentary in indented small print, visually distinct from the main text — eight times on this day (printed pp. 11 ×2, 17, 21, 22, 24, 25 ×2, 27).
items.site_html: All eight are rendered as ordinary body paragraphs. grep -rn 'neave_note' content/days/day-09/ returns zero hits.
items.evidence_html: Day 10 uses neave_note 19 times and Day 11 uses it 20 — the same source material, the same typographic device, the immediately adjacent days. Day 9 uses it not once, so the source's distinction between Neave's commentary and the main narrative is flattened throughout. That is a real difference from the source and worth fixing, but it touches eight paragraphs across four files and is a presentation decision rather than a wording one, so it is raised here rather than folded into this pass's diff. (D9-29 is the subset that is also a mis-attribution and is proposed as a fix.)
items.outcome: Raised as #798 — Day 9 renders all eight of Neave’s small-print insets as ordinary body text, 2026-09-12.

items.chip: Day 3 is also missing its approvals page

items.site_html: Audited across all nine: Days 1 (6 notes), 5, 6, 11, the Appendix and Contributions all carry theirs; Day 7's is <mark class='gone'>reworded and has lost its page reference</mark>; <mark class='gone'>Days 3 and 9 carry nothing at all</mark>. Five different presentational shapes are in use.
items.evidence_html: Day 9's own gap is proposed as a fix (D9-34). Day 3 is the only other surface missing it outright — two notes covering the Ford Motor Company diagrams (approved by Bill Scherkenbach) and quotations from Understanding Statistical Process Control (SPC Press Inc). Day 3's Wave 2 pass has not run yet, so it will be caught there, but three closed passes (Days 6, 11, 1) went by without anyone checking the approvals page existed at all — and there is no single thing to grep for, because five different shapes are in use across the nine surfaces. Raised as a corpus-wide issue rather than absorbed here. Nothing to apply on Day 9 beyond D9-34.
items.outcome: Raised as #796 — corpus-wide audit of all nine approvals pages, 2026-09-12.
